ssh_notes: Instance 37161678 on ssh7.vast.ai:11678 (public IP 222.230.13.166, Japan JP, machine_id 31089 host_id 45726 -- IDENTICAL physical machine to t0114's selection). The Vast.ai SSH proxy auto-attaches a tmux session on TTY logins -- this is disabled for this instance via 'touch /root/.no_auto_tmux' built into the create-instance --onstart-cmd. After that, non-TTY 'ssh -i /c/Users/md1avn/.ssh/id_ed25519 -p 11678 root@ssh7.vast.ai <cmd>' works for stdin-piped commands and run_with_logs wrappers. SSH key on this Windows host is at /c/Users/md1avn/.ssh/id_ed25519 (NOT ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 because '~' resolves to U:/ which is an unmounted network drive). For Vast.ai key attachment: the registered key id 855344 (clean comment 'md1avn-t0113') has identical key material to the local file -- no additional 'vastai attach ssh' call was needed because the onstart-cmd injects the clean key comment 'md1avn-t0115' into /root/.ssh/authorized_keys directly. The legacy id 801863 with comment 'shefuniad\md1avn@TEN00BE4360B45A' (which IS the literal local file comment) is NOT used because the literal backslash in the comment field corrupts key parsing on the Vast.ai SSH proxy (root cause of t0113's setup-time SSH failure 660-second delay). The t0114 key id 856172 ('md1avn-t0114') was deleted between tasks; we did not need to create a t0115 key because the onstart-cmd handles authorized_keys directly. PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 and PYTHONUTF8=1 must be set in the local shell when running pip/ssh commands wrapped in run_with_logs; otherwise run_with_logs.py crashes on non-UTF-8 output from the remote. Note the cosmetic 'Welcome to vast.ai' banner is appended to every command's stderr by the Vast.ai login wrapper -- treat as benign. SSH worked on the first attempt (no key-attach retry needed).

mod_compile.note_on_load_mechanisms: Modern NEURON places libnrnmech.so directly in x86_64/ (not in x86_64/.libs/ as older versions did). 'load_mechanisms(x86_64)' from Python returns False because it looks for the legacy path, but hasattr(h, 'bkt80') etc. all return True because NEURON auto-loads x86_64/libnrnmech.so from CWD on import. This matches t0112's, t0113's, and t0114's observation exactly. Library size 118704 bytes is byte-identical to t0114's library size (same Linux ABI, same Zen-3 Milan target, same NEURON 8.2.7 build, same machine_id 31089).
